focus: Left Achilles insertion (micro-tearing, orthopedist 10/2) + left post tib / arch

phase.name: Rebuild capacity
phase.exit: Heel-raise test PASSED 10/11 (20 each leg, left harder and less stable). Remaining: pain-free two-footed hops 2×10. Then Phase 3: springs (pogo hops → skips → single-leg hops).

note: About 15 min daily at home. Achilles has been quiet all week, so loading moves up: standing heel raises replace the seated-only work. Pain during and the morning after stay at or under 3/10.
pain_rules: Green: at or under 3/10 during, and settled by the next morning, continue. Yellow: 4–5/10 or a worse morning, drop back a level for 2–3 days. Red: sharp pain, a giving-way moment, or swelling, stop that exercise and call the orthopedist.
special: Running is back in, carefully: short easy runs, flat, never on back-to-back days, gated on the Achilles being quiet that morning and after the last run. Still keep the heel up (shoes with a heel, no barefoot), no left calf stretching, no heel drops off a step, no hills or incline. If it gives way again or gets worse, stop running and call the orthopedist.

exercises.name: Standing heel raises
exercises.cue: Left only now (it passed 20 reps). Always do the left first and have the right match its reps, so the strong side doesn't outwork the weak one. 2 s up, pause, 3 s down, stop when the heel touches the floor. When 3×15 is easy, hold a dumbbell and drop to 3×8–10. Never off a step.

exercises.name: Seated soleus raise
exercises.cue: Seated, knees bent, heavier dumbbells on the knees. 2 s up, 3 s down, stop at the floor. Trains the deep calf that takes most of the running load.

exercises.name: Isometric heel-raise hold
exercises.cue: Half height, push the balls of the feet down. Use as the warm-up before the standing raises and before runs.

exercises.name: Short-foot arch doming
exercises.cue: Pull the big-toe knuckle toward the heel, no toe curling. End the rep when the dome starts collapsing.

exercises.name: Isometric inversion hold
exercises.cue: Seated, foot flat. Push the inside edge of the foot inward against your other foot or a wall. Moderate effort, pain-free. Keeps the post tib working.

exercises.name: Tibialis raises
exercises.cue: Stand upright with your back on a wall and heels about a foot out, lift both forefeet. Small, controlled range; don't lean back far.

exercises.name: Side plank + top-leg raise
exercises.cue: Hips stacked, lift the top leg while holding the plank. Hip control is part of the fix.

exercises.name: Single-leg balance
exercises.cue: Extra set on the left: it's the less stable side. In shoes, firm floor, fingertips near a counter. Progress to eyes closed when 30 s is steady.

exercises.name: Right-leg range work
exercises.cue: Right calf stretch straight-knee and bent-knee, 45s each. The left gets no calf stretching.

also: Film one set of single-leg heel raises from behind each Sunday: phone ~3 ft back at heel height, good light, a marker line down the back of each heel, slow reps (2 s up, pause, 3 s down), send the original file
Massage: calf and soleus only. No deep work, scraping, or cupping on the heel or the low Achilles

Foot rolling (knobby ball), once a day, seated: arch 1–2 min/foot at up to 6/10, bottom of the heel gently, inside of the heel light. Never on the back of the heel where the Achilles attaches. Follow with doming or heel-raise holds
Desk and commute: every 30–45 min do 10 ankle pumps and a few doming holds, or stand and walk a minute

Collagen (your pick: bovine hide peptides, 10 g/scoop): 1–1½ scoops + ~50 mg vitamin C (small orange) 30–60 min before the rehab session or a strength day. At least 30–60 min after thyroid medication; multivitamin ~4 h away. It adds to your pea protein, not instead of it
Evening: Normatec and/or cold plunge if it helps the heel settle
Protein stays high (155 g/day) for tendon repair; don't deepen the calorie deficit while healing

Sundays: single-leg heel raise count each side, knee-to-wall in cm, morning stiffness minutes, any giving-way moments. Baseline 9/28: knee-to-wall L 9.5 (Achilles-limited), R 11. Test 10/11: single-leg heel raises L 20 / R 20, left harder and less stable
avoid: Jumping, hopping (except Sunday's test), pickleball, speed work, back-to-back running days
Any left calf stretching; heel drops off a step; deep squats, lunges, step-ups
Hills, StairMaster, incline treadmill walking, bike climbs or standing on the pedals, jump rope
Barefoot walking, flat shoes, flip-flops, the plated Hyperion
Single-leg balance on soft surfaces (yoga mats, pillows, foam pads)
